column2: Grant the Crown's Apostolic Charter

Place Catholic schools, missions and charitable houses under the Bourbon crown's patronage. The charter supports religious instruction throughout the kingdom and permits regional mission grants in Africa. Moralism sustains the programme. A religious-freedom settlement prevents this privileged charter until the existing guarantees have been reconsidered.
The Crown and the Apostolate

The Bourbon standard now commands a united Italy, and the court means its Catholic institutions to accompany that national authority. Bishops, teaching orders and charitable houses receive a royal charter for instruction and missionary work. Their supporters speak of restoring the Christian communities of the southern Mediterranean. Ministers see another task: schools, hospitals and dependable local offices must give substance to promises made beneath the royal arms. The charter sponsors persuasion and religious education through continuing institutions. It does not remake the inhabitants by proclamation. Its privileges depend upon the crown's religious policy, and existing guarantees of religious freedom remain a separate obligation.
Publish the instructions and record the programme.
Withdraw the Crown's Apostolic Privileges
Withdraw the national privileges of the missionary charter. Regional mission support will cease while the schools and houses already established remain part of local life.
Patronato Apostolico della Corona
Royal patronage sustains Catholic instruction and missionary institutions while the crown maintains its Catholic and moralist policy.
The Missionary Charter Is Suspended

The government's present institutions or religious policy no longer sustain the privileges promised by the apostolic charter. The treasury suspends national patronage. Mission houses must rely on their own arrangements until the charter's governing conditions return.
Publish the instructions and record the programme.
The Apostolic Charter Resumes

The crown again sustains the institutions under which the apostolic charter was granted. Its national patronage resumes, and the provincial offices may renew support for mission houses whose existing grants remain recorded.
Publish the instructions and record the programme.
Open the Settler Routes to Tunisia

Invite Italian farming families, fishermen and artisans to the incorporated districts of Tunisia. Supervised passage, agricultural credit and prepared workplaces offer a future beneath Italian civil law. The programme applies to cored districts under Italian control.
Verso le Terre d'Oltremare

Passenger lists now reach the offices at Naples and Palermo. Farmers seek a holding of their own, fishermen ask about the harbours, and craftsmen hope to find work where new streets and workshops are taking shape. The crown calls these departures a national undertaking: Italian homes beyond the sea, joined to the homeland by regular shipping and a common civil administration. Officials in Tunisia must prepare workplaces and examine land titles before promising a livelihood. Public credit and inspected contracts support settlement without declaring the country empty. Arrival will depend upon employment, security and the choices of the families who decide to take passage.

Supervised passages, prepared workplaces and agricultural credit invite settlers to an incorporated Italian district across the Mediterranean.
The Settler Routes Reach New Districts
Further incorporated districts have become available to the settlement offices. The existing programme extends to their workplaces and passage arrangements under Italian civil administration.

Entrust the Missions in Tunisia to the Church

Grant Catholic orders provincial support for mission houses, religious instruction and charitable schools in Tunisia. The programme requires direct Italian administration and the crown's active apostolic charter. Regional grants extend as further districts pass under Italian control.
The Mission Houses of Tunisia

The royal charter has reached Tunisia. Catholic orders prepare teaching rooms, dispensaries and mission houses under the protection of the Italian administration. At court the undertaking is celebrated as a renewal of the Christian Mediterranean. Provincial officials must turn that language into appointments, supplies and regular accounts. Local Muslim and Jewish communities watch the new privileges closely, while the clergy hopes that instruction and charitable work will win adherents. Religious change proceeds through the inhabitants and their institutions over time. The ministry keeps this provincial grant distinct from settlement, citizenship and the ordinary courts.
Publish the instructions and record the programme.
Missioni della Quarta Sponda
Provincial grants sustain Catholic mission houses and instruction under the crown's active apostolic charter.
The Provincial Mission Grant Extends

The mission offices will extend the provincial grant already authorised by the crown to further districts under direct Italian control. Appointments and supplies remain subject to the existing charter.
